topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under RCW 18.85.011(10), how can a natural person qualify as a "designated broker" without being designated by a separate business entity?
choice_a: By being the natural person who owns a sole proprietorship real estate firm
choice_b: By passing the managing broker exam with a perfect score
choice_c: By having ten years of licensed real estate experience
choice_d: By being appointed branch manager of the firm
explanation: RCW 18.85.011(10) defines "designated broker" to include a natural person who owns a sole proprietorship real estate firm, as an alternative to the controlling-interest-plus-designation route used by entity firms.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under RCW 18.85.011(10), when a real estate firm is organized as a corporation, LLC, LLP, or partnership, what two things must be true of the natural person designated as its designated broker?
choice_a: The person must have a controlling interest in the firm and be designated by the firm to act as designated broker
choice_b: The person must be the firm's youngest licensed managing broker and work part-time
choice_c: The person must own no interest in the firm and be elected by client vote
choice_d: The person must be a corporate officer only, regardless of real estate license status
explanation: RCW 18.85.011(10) defines a designated broker of an entity firm as a natural person with a controlling interest in the firm who is designated by the entity to act as designated broker on its behalf.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under RCW 18.85.011(15), a managing broker performs real estate brokerage services under whose supervision, and may in turn supervise whom?
choice_a: Under the supervision of the designated broker, and may supervise other brokers or managing brokers licensed to the firm
choice_b: Under the supervision of the county assessor, and may supervise title company employees
choice_c: Under no supervision at all once managing-broker licensed
choice_d: Under the supervision of the buyer's attorney, and may supervise escrow officers
explanation: RCW 18.85.011(15) defines a managing broker as acting under the supervision of the designated broker, while being permitted to supervise other brokers or managing brokers licensed to the firm.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under RCW 18.85.111(3), to how many firms may a managing broker's license be affiliated at any one time, and how does that differ from the designated broker registration rule in RCW 18.85.121(1)?
choice_a: One firm only under the managing broker's license, even though the same person may separately register as designated broker for more than one firm
choice_b: Unlimited firms, identical to the designated broker rule
choice_c: Exactly two firms, one more than the designated broker limit
choice_d: Zero firms; a managing broker license does not attach to any specific firm
explanation: RCW 18.85.111(3) limits a managing broker's underlying license to one firm at a time, which is distinct from the designated-broker endorsement under RCW 18.85.121(1) that allows the same person to register as designated broker for multiple firms.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under RCW 18.85.291, where must a real estate broker's and managing broker's licenses be kept at all times, and what happens to the license when the licensee stops representing the firm?
choice_a: The licenses are kept by the firm, and the license ceases to be in force when the broker or managing broker stops representing the firm
choice_b: The licenses are kept by the licensee personally at home, and remain in force indefinitely regardless of affiliation
choice_c: The licenses are kept by the county recorder, and never expire
choice_d: The licenses are kept by the client, and expire only at contract closing
explanation: RCW 18.85.291 requires brokers' and managing brokers' licenses to be kept at all times by their firm, and provides that the license ceases to be in force once the licensee ceases to represent the firm.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under RCW 18.85.291, after a broker's or managing broker's license is surrendered upon termination, what may the director do if the broker or managing broker applies and pays the prescribed fee?
choice_a: Issue a new license for the unexpired term, if the broker or managing broker is otherwise entitled to it
choice_b: Require the broker to retake the full licensing examination before any new license issues
choice_c: Permanently bar reissuance until the next full renewal cycle
choice_d: Automatically transfer the license to the new firm without any application
explanation: RCW 18.85.291 provides that, upon application and payment of the prescribed fee, the director shall issue a new license for the unexpired term if the broker or managing broker is otherwise entitled to it.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under RCW 18.85.275(3), beyond delegating duties to a managing broker, what recordkeeping obligation does the designated broker have regarding the firm's managing brokers?
choice_a: The designated broker must maintain a record of the firm's managing brokers and any delegations made to them
choice_b: No recordkeeping obligation exists once a delegation agreement is signed
choice_c: The obligation to maintain such records falls solely on the department of licensing
choice_d: The record must be destroyed after one year to protect licensee privacy
explanation: RCW 18.85.275(3) requires the designated broker to maintain a record of the firm's managing brokers and of delegations made to managing brokers, in addition to being permitted to delegate certain duties.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under RCW 18.85.275(4), in addition to contract authority, what authority does the designated broker hold regarding licensees joining the firm?
choice_a: The authority to accept new or transferred licensees to represent the real estate firm
choice_b: The authority to unilaterally revoke any licensee's state license
choice_c: The authority to set the statewide managing broker examination curriculum
choice_d: No such authority; only the department may accept new licensees
explanation: RCW 18.85.275(4) gives the designated broker authority to accept new or transferred licensees to represent the real estate firm, alongside the authority to amend, bind, or terminate brokerage service contracts.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: A designated broker delegates trust account reconciliation duties to a managing broker under RCW 18.85.275(3). If the managing broker fails to complete the monthly reconciliation, does that delegation relieve the designated broker of responsibility for supervising compliance?
choice_a: No -- RCW 18.85.275(1) still charges the designated broker with supervising compliance, and WAC 308-124C-125 still requires the designated broker to ensure the reconciliation is completed
choice_b: Yes -- once a duty is delegated, the designated broker has no further supervisory role
choice_c: Only the department of licensing can be held responsible in that scenario
choice_d: Responsibility shifts entirely to the client whose funds were affected
explanation: Delegation under RCW 18.85.275(3) does not eliminate the designated broker's underlying supervisory duty under RCW 18.85.275(1), and WAC 308-124C-125(4)-(6) separately obligates the designated broker to ensure monthly trust account reconciliations and trial balances are completed and in balance.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: A sole proprietorship real estate firm is owned outright by one individual who holds a managing broker's license. Under RCW 18.85.011(10), does that owner automatically qualify as the firm's designated broker without a separate designation by a business entity?
choice_a: Yes -- the statutory definition of designated broker separately includes a natural person who owns a sole proprietorship real estate firm
choice_b: No -- sole proprietors can never serve as designated broker
choice_c: No -- only corporations may have a designated broker
choice_d: Yes, but only after ten years of licensure
explanation: RCW 18.85.011(10) defines "designated broker" to include the natural person who owns a sole proprietorship real estate firm, distinct from the controlling-interest-plus-entity-designation route that applies to corporations, LLCs, LLPs, and partnerships.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-125(1), the designated broker's responsibility to assure brokerage services comply with chapters 18.85, 18.86, and 18.235 RCW applies to which services?
choice_a: All real estate brokerage services in which the designated broker personally participated
choice_b: Only services performed by the newest licensee at the firm
choice_c: Only services involving commercial property
choice_d: Only services that generated a written complaint
explanation: WAC 308-124C-125(1) requires the designated broker to assure that all real estate brokerage services in which he or she participated comply with chapters 18.85, 18.86, and 18.235 RCW and their implementing rules.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-125(2), what must a designated broker do when the department conducts an investigation, audit, or licensing matter involving the firm?
choice_a: Cooperate with the department
choice_b: Retain independent legal counsel before responding to any department request
choice_c: Refer all department inquiries exclusively to the firm's managing brokers
choice_d: Take no action unless a subpoena is issued
explanation: WAC 308-124C-125(2) lists cooperating with the department in an investigation, audit, or licensing matter among the designated broker's core responsibilities.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-125(3), what must the designated broker ensure regarding the firm's offices and required records?
choice_a: They are accessible to the director's authorized representatives, with copies of required records made available upon demand
choice_b: They are sealed and available only pursuant to a court subpoena
choice_c: They may be withheld until the firm's attorney reviews them
choice_d: They must be physically relocated to Olympia for inspection
explanation: WAC 308-124C-125(3) requires the designated broker to ensure accessibility of the firm's offices and records to the director's authorized representatives, and to make copies of required records available upon demand.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-125(4) through (6), even before any duty is delegated, what must the designated broker ensure is completed monthly for the firm's trust bank accounts?
choice_a: Reconciliations and trial balances that are complete, accurate, up-to-date, and that show the accounts are in balance
choice_b: A single annual reconciliation performed by an outside CPA
choice_c: A trial balance only, with no reconciliation required
choice_d: Nothing; this duty applies only to managing brokers, never to the designated broker
explanation: WAC 308-124C-125(4)-(6) makes the designated broker responsible for ensuring monthly trust bank account reconciliations and trial balances are completed, accurate, up-to-date, and show the accounts in balance.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-125(7), what must the designated broker ensure is in place regarding customer or client funds or property?
choice_a: Policies or procedures to account for their safe handling
choice_b: A firm-wide ban on ever holding client funds
choice_c: A requirement that all funds be held by the client's lender instead of the firm
choice_d: A requirement that funds be converted to cashier's checks before deposit
explanation: WAC 308-124C-125(7) requires the designated broker to ensure policies or procedures are in place to account for the safe handling of customer or client funds or property.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-125(8)(a), to whom may a designated broker delegate duties by written agreement?
choice_a: Only to managing brokers licensed to the firm
choice_b: To any licensed broker in the state, regardless of firm affiliation
choice_c: To unlicensed administrative staff
choice_d: To the firm's outside accountant
explanation: WAC 308-124C-125(8)(a) restricts delegation of designated broker duties to managing brokers who are licensed to the firm.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-125(9)(b), the designated broker's written policy must address levels of supervision for which categories of firm personnel?
choice_a: All brokers, managing brokers, and branch managers of the firm
choice_b: Only unlicensed clerical employees
choice_c: Only brokers who work part-time
choice_d: Only the designated broker's own direct hires, excluding branch personnel
explanation: WAC 308-124C-125(9)(b) requires the designated broker's written policy to address levels of supervision for all brokers, managing brokers, and branch managers of the firm.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-125(10), the designated broker must ensure that which persons performing real estate brokerage services on behalf of the firm are appropriately licensed?
choice_a: All such persons, as well as the firm itself
choice_b: Only brokers who joined the firm within the last year
choice_c: Only managing brokers, not the firm entity
choice_d: Only persons who directly handle client trust funds
explanation: WAC 308-124C-125(10) requires the designated broker to ensure that all persons performing real estate brokerage services on the firm's behalf, and the firm itself, are appropriately licensed.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-125(11), within how many business days of mutual acceptance must affiliated licensees submit their transaction documents, and to whom?
choice_a: Two business days, to the designated broker, branch manager, or delegated managing broker
choice_b: Ten business days, to the client's title company
choice_c: Thirty calendar days, to the department of licensing directly
choice_d: One business day, to the county recorder
explanation: WAC 308-124C-125(11) requires the designated broker to ensure affiliated licensees submit their transaction documents to the designated broker, branch manager, or delegated managing broker within two business days of mutual acceptance.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-125(12), the designated broker's duty to remain knowledgeable extends to which bodies of law?
choice_a: Chapters 18.85, 18.86, and 18.235 RCW and their related rules
choice_b: Only the federal Fair Housing Act
choice_c: Only local zoning ordinances
choice_d: Only the firm's internal employee handbook
explanation: WAC 308-124C-125(12) requires the designated broker to be knowledgeable of chapters 18.85, 18.86, and 18.235 RCW and their related rules.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-135(1), a managing broker must assure that which real estate brokerage services comply with chapters 18.85, 18.86, and 18.235 RCW?
choice_a: All such services in which the managing broker personally participated
choice_b: Only services performed by brokers with less than two years of experience
choice_c: Only services involving client trust funds
choice_d: Only services performed at the firm's main office
explanation: WAC 308-124C-135(1) requires a managing broker to assure that all real estate brokerage services in which he or she participated comply with chapters 18.85, 18.86, and 18.235 RCW and their rules.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-135(3), a managing broker must be knowledgeable of which statutes and related rules?
choice_a: Chapters 18.85, 18.86, and 18.235 RCW
choice_b: Only the Uniform Commercial Code
choice_c: Only chapter 18.235 RCW, since chapter 18.85 RCW applies solely to designated brokers
choice_d: Only federal RESPA regulations
explanation: WAC 308-124C-135(3) requires managing brokers to be knowledgeable of chapters 18.85, 18.86, and 18.235 RCW and their related rules -- the same body of law the designated broker must know under WAC 308-124C-125(12).

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-135(4), what administrative obligation does a managing broker have regarding their mailing address?
choice_a: Keeping the real estate program informed of their current mailing address
choice_b: Filing a change-of-address form with the county assessor
choice_c: Posting their address publicly on the firm's website
choice_d: No obligation exists unless the address change affects licensure eligibility
explanation: WAC 308-124C-135(4) requires a managing broker to keep the real estate program informed of his or her current mailing address.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-135(5) and (6), a managing broker's own responsibilities include following whose written home inspector referral policy, and maintaining what license status?
choice_a: The designated broker's written policy, while being appropriately licensed
choice_b: The client's preferred policy, while being licensed as a broker only
choice_c: The department's model policy, while holding a firm license
choice_d: No specific policy applies to managing brokers, only to brokers
explanation: WAC 308-124C-135(5)-(6) requires a managing broker to follow the designated broker's written home inspector referral policy and to remain appropriately licensed.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-135(8), a managing broker's own responsibilities include following licensing laws and rules regarding which four areas?
choice_a: Safe handling of customer/client funds and property, timely delivery of those funds/property, proper and legal advertising, and modifying or terminating brokerage service contracts on behalf of the firm
choice_b: Building code compliance, parking regulations, signage permits, and property tax assessments
choice_c: Employment law, workers' compensation, unemployment insurance, and payroll tax withholding
choice_d: Federal securities law, antitrust law, banking regulations, and consumer credit reporting
explanation: WAC 308-124C-135(8) requires managing brokers to follow licensing laws and rules regarding safe handling and timely delivery of customer/client funds and property, proper and legal advertising, and modifying or terminating brokerage service contracts on the firm's behalf.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-137(6), when this duty is delegated by the designated broker, what must the managing broker ensure about the firm's advertising?
choice_a: That it is proper and legal
choice_b: That it appears exclusively in print media
choice_c: That it is pre-approved by the department before publication
choice_d: That it excludes any mention of price
explanation: WAC 308-124C-137(6) makes a managing broker with delegated authority responsible for ensuring that the firm's advertising is proper and legal.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-137(7), a managing broker with delegated authority must ensure what regarding brokerage service contracts?
choice_a: Timely review of contracts
choice_b: That contracts are notarized before signing
choice_c: That contracts are reviewed only at year-end
choice_d: That contracts are reviewed exclusively by outside counsel
explanation: WAC 308-124C-137(7) requires a managing broker with delegated authority to ensure timely review of brokerage service contracts.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-137(9), a managing broker with delegated supervisory authority must ensure that persons employed, contracted, or representing the firm under that delegated authority are what?
choice_a: Appropriately licensed
choice_b: Provided a company vehicle
choice_c: Assigned exclusively to residential listings
choice_d: Covered by a separate malpractice policy purchased personally by the managing broker
explanation: WAC 308-124C-137(9) requires a managing broker with delegated authority to ensure that persons employed, contracted, or representing the firm under that delegated supervision are appropriately licensed.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-137(10), a managing broker with delegated supervisory duties must ensure that brokers and managing brokers under that supervision submit their transaction documents to whom, and within what time frame?
choice_a: To the designated broker or delegated managing broker, within two business days of mutual acceptance
choice_b: To the escrow company, within five calendar days of closing
choice_c: To the department of licensing, within thirty days of listing
choice_d: To the buyer's lender, within one business day of the offer
explanation: WAC 308-124C-137(10) requires a managing broker with delegated authority to ensure that brokers and managing brokers under their supervision submit transaction documents to the designated broker or delegated managing broker within two business days of mutual acceptance.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-137(12), a managing broker with delegated authority must ensure what regarding the firm's offices and records?
choice_a: Accessibility to the director's authorized representatives, with copies of required records made available upon demand
choice_b: That records are destroyed after each closed transaction
choice_c: That records are accessible only to the firm's designated broker, never to state regulators
choice_d: That records are stored exclusively in paper form
explanation: WAC 308-124C-137(12) requires a managing broker with delegated authority to ensure accessibility of the firm's offices and records to the director's authorized representatives, with copies made available upon demand -- mirroring the designated broker's own duty under WAC 308-124C-125(3).

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-145(2)(a), during a broker's first two years of licensure, that broker must participate in what, conducted by the designated broker or appointed managing broker?
choice_a: All required reviews of real estate brokerage agreements and services
choice_b: A single review conducted only at the two-year licensure anniversary
choice_c: Peer reviews conducted by other brokers who also have less than two years of experience
choice_d: An annual bonus review unrelated to transaction files
explanation: WAC 308-124C-145(2)(a) requires a broker in the first two years of licensure to participate in all required reviews of real estate brokerage agreements and services conducted by the designated broker or appointed managing broker.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-145(2)(b), a broker in their first two years of licensure must submit evidence of completing what to the designated broker or appointed managing broker?
choice_a: Department-required clock hour education courses
choice_b: A criminal background check renewed annually
choice_c: A personal financial disclosure statement
choice_d: A signed noncompete agreement
explanation: WAC 308-124C-145(2)(b) requires a broker in the first two years of licensure to submit evidence of completion of department-required clock hour education courses to the designated broker or appointed managing broker.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-145(2)(c), what must a broker in their first two years of licensure do when offering brokerage services beyond their level of expertise?
choice_a: Secure advice or assistance from the designated broker or appointed managing broker
choice_b: Decline to represent the client and refer them to a competitor firm
choice_c: Proceed without disclosure since supervision is optional for that service type
choice_d: Wait until the two-year heightened supervision period ends before proceeding
explanation: WAC 308-124C-145(2)(c) requires a broker in the first two years of licensure to secure advice or assistance from the designated broker or appointed managing broker when offering brokerage services beyond the broker's level of expertise.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-145(2)(d), a broker in their first two years of licensure must timely submit brokerage service contracts, documents, and funds to the appropriate managing broker or designated broker in accordance with what?
choice_a: The designated broker's document and contract review policy
choice_b: Whatever schedule the individual broker personally prefers
choice_c: A schedule set unilaterally by the client
choice_d: The buyer's lender's underwriting timeline
explanation: WAC 308-124C-145(2)(d) requires timely submission of brokerage service contracts, documents, and funds to the appropriate managing broker or designated broker, in accordance with the designated broker's document and contract review policy.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: A broker who has been licensed for eighteen months wants to offer a brokerage service beyond their current level of expertise. Under WAC 308-124C-145(2)(c), what must that broker do first?
choice_a: Secure advice or assistance from the designated broker or appointed managing broker
choice_b: Nothing; the two-year heightened supervision period does not apply to this scenario
choice_c: Obtain a separate state license specific to that service type
choice_d: Wait an additional six months before offering any new service type
explanation: Because the broker is still within the first two years of licensure, WAC 308-124C-145(2)(c) requires securing advice or assistance from the designated broker or appointed managing broker before offering services beyond the broker's expertise.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-130(6), what supervisory role does a branch manager have over personnel at the branch office?
choice_a: Overseeing the branch's licensees, employees, and contractors
choice_b: Overseeing only the branch's unlicensed receptionist
choice_c: No oversight role; that authority rests solely with the firm's designated broker
choice_d: Overseeing personnel only at the firm's main office, not the branch
explanation: WAC 308-124C-130(6) charges the branch manager with overseeing the branch's licensees, employees, and contractors.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-130(8), a branch manager's responsibilities include what personnel actions specific to the branch?
choice_a: Hiring, transferring, and releasing licensees to and from the branch
choice_b: Setting statewide firm compensation policy
choice_c: Approving the designated broker's own continuing education plan
choice_d: Certifying the firm's annual tax return
explanation: WAC 308-124C-130(8) gives the branch manager responsibility for hiring, transferring, and releasing licensees to and from the branch office.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-130(9), a branch manager's oversight of the branch office includes supervision of brokers and managing brokers, plus what heightened obligation?
choice_a: Heightened supervision of brokers licensed for less than two years
choice_b: A requirement to personally close every branch transaction
choice_c: A requirement to review only commercial transactions
choice_d: No heightened obligation exists at the branch level
explanation: WAC 308-124C-130(9) requires the branch manager to oversee all branch activity, including supervision of brokers and managing brokers and heightened supervision of brokers licensed for less than two years -- paralleling the heightened-supervision duty imposed elsewhere on the designated and managing broker.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: Under WAC 308-124C-130(7), a branch manager must ensure affiliated licensees at the branch submit their transaction documents to whom, and within what period?
choice_a: To the designated broker or delegated managing broker, within two business days of mutual acceptance
choice_b: To the branch's landlord, within thirty calendar days
choice_c: To the local MLS, within one business day
choice_d: To the client directly, with no fixed deadline
explanation: WAC 308-124C-130(7) requires the branch manager to ensure affiliated licensees at the branch submit their transaction documents to the designated broker or delegated managing broker within two business days of mutual acceptance.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: According to the Department of Licensing, what does "controlling interest" mean for purposes of qualifying as a designated broker?
choice_a: The ability to control the operational and/or financial decisions of the firm, whether or not the person has an ownership interest
choice_b: Owning at least 51 percent of the firm's stock, with no exceptions
choice_c: Holding the title of company president regardless of actual decision-making authority
choice_d: Having the largest individual commission volume at the firm
explanation: The department's designated broker guidance defines controlling interest as the ability to control the operational and/or financial decisions of the firm; the designated broker must be granted controlling interest whether or not they hold an ownership interest.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: According to the Department of Licensing, how long does a designated broker endorsement last before it expires?
choice_a: It expires with the managing broker's license two years after it is issued
choice_b: It never expires once granted
choice_c: It expires after six months and must be renewed quarterly
choice_d: It expires only if the firm changes its business name
explanation: The department's designated broker guidance states the endorsement expires with the license two years after it is issued.

topic: WA Managing Broker: Designated Broker & Supervisory Authority
question: According to the Department of Licensing, how does a firm designate someone as its designated broker?
choice_a: The firm uses an online process to select the designated broker when the firm is first licensed or to replace an outgoing designated broker
choice_b: The department randomly assigns a designated broker from a waiting list
choice_c: The designated broker role is inherited automatically by the firm's most senior broker
choice_d: A designated broker is elected by a vote of all the firm's clients
explanation: The department's designated broker guidance describes an online selection process used when a firm is first licensed or when it needs to replace an outgoing designated broker.
